postings.title: Electrical/Mechanical Technician
postings.description:
(also advertised as Mechatronic Technician) 

A little bit about us   

At Recycleye we are revolutionising Recycling. Our ground-breaking AI powers robots and optical sorters making waste sorting faster, cleaner and more profitable. With our advanced tech, the previously unsortable can now be sorted efficiently and effectively. Founded in 2019, we have grown rapidly ever since, with installations at leading waste management companies across Europe and the US. We are on a mission to help our clients produce higher quality outputs – turning the world’s waste into valuable resource. And our work has never been needed more. Worldwide only 9% of plastic waste is being recycled – every day, we are proud to work on making a meaningful difference towards a sustainable future.

Be part of it – come and join us!  

Why choose to work at Recycleye?

 Our team works together to grow and succeed, driven by our shared values of empowerment, inclusivity, and perseverance. We offer great benefits (which we think punch above our weight), built-in upskilling and unlimited holiday (yes, really).   We know that our mission will be achieved by having the most passionate, driven, talented, and all-around best people on our team. So come and shape the future and help turn trash into treasure! 

The opportunity

This role will involve becoming a key member of our production team, working closely with Technicians, Project Managers and Engineers. The role will be flexible to the needs of the team, some weeks focusing more on a project build we might have in-house, other weeks focusing on improving the efficiency of our workshop, working on making ourselves more efficient. 

We offer:

- High ownership and autonomy  

- Fast-paced scale-up environment with real engineering challenges  

- Opportunity to shape processes, standards, and best practices  

- Exposure to full product lifecycle and customer deployments  

- Occasional travel (UK and Europe) to customer sites for installations and troubleshooting (once per month)

Responsibilities

- Electrical assembly and quality testing, in workshop and on-site 

- Mechanical assembly, quality testing and installation of our QuantiSort and QualiBot offerings

- Development, building and testing of the subassemblies that make up all our product streams  

- Maintaining component traceability and ensuring the highest quality standards 

- Troubleshoot and resolve any assembly issues or discrepancies to maintain production schedules whilst communicating this information back into improving the process 

Requirements

- 4+ years of experience in a hands-on technician role in an industrial engineering environment

- Power and control wiring aptitude a must

- Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics with the ability to report errors or oversights

- Strong problem-solving mentality for engineering challenges 

- Ability to interpret engineering information in multiple formats, including assembly instructions, 2D drawings, 3D CAD assemblies 

- Route and terminate pneumatic lines, wiring/cabling and electrical conduit 

- Confidence using  workshop and power tools, with knowledge of safe handling 

- Keen eye for detail, both in following and developing processes with a proven ability to identify and implement improvements

- Willingness to deal with ambiguity as we grow, and input to iterate and improve building process and design 

- Open to occasional weekend work (with time in lieu) 

- Based within a commutable distance to Stratford, London, to work onsite 5 days a week 

- Good communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively 

It’s a bonus if you have 

- Familiarity or training on electrical standards e.g. BS 7671 and 60204

- Experience assembling and testing pneumatic systems

- Experience installing industrial equipment and warehouse management 

- Experience improving health and safety processes 

- Prior ERP/inventory management experience

- Startup or scale-up experience  

- Full clean driving license 

- Forklift qualifications

Even if you don’t tick every box listed above but are motivated by our work and believe you can make a difference on our team, we’d really love to hear from you – so please do apply and drop us a note about what you bring! We are particularly interested in hearing from you if your background enables you to bring a different perspective to our team. 

Benefits

- Progression: we are growing rapidly and excited for you to make an impact as we do so

- Unlimited holiday

- A welcoming and inclusive team environment with monthly company-wide socials

- Plenty of opportunities for training and personal development

- Healthcare coverage – Vitality is available from your very first day!

postings.title: Interested in joining Recycleye
postings.description:
At Recycleye, we are turning the world’s waste into resource. According to the OECD, only 9% of waste has ever been recycled – but we’re changing that through our development of AI-based sensors combined with robotics that identify and sort a wide range of recyclables. We are transforming the economics behind the $2.5 trillion global waste recycling industry, and we want you to join us!

Founded in 2019, we have experienced rapid growth with technology deployed across Europe and the US and are on a trajectory to continue scaling at pace. To do this, we need more innovators to join our team.

We work together to grow and succeed, driven by our values of empowerment, inclusivity, and perseverance. We want you to come and join our vision of delivering improved efficiency and purity to waste sorting, turning rubbish into a trove of resources.

So come and shape the future and help turn trash into treasure! 

The role

As a Junior Technician, you'll help build, test, and install our products: QuantiSort, our AI-powered airjet sorting system, and QualiBot, our robotic sorting system. You'll work closely with the rest of the Production team (Technicians, Project Managers, and Engineers), building hands-on experience in mechanical and electrical assembly, and playing an active part in improving our processes as the company scales.

What you'll do

- Assemble, test, and install our electro-mechanical systems in our workshop and at customer sites.

- Maintain component traceability and uphold high quality standards throughout production.

- Troubleshoot assembly issues and discrepancies to keep production on schedule, and feed what you learn back into improving our processes.

- Help organise and develop our workshop and production hall so we can deliver multiple product lines efficiently.

- Keep the workshop and production hall clean, safe, and organised.

What we're looking for

- A relevant qualification (such as a BTEC, HNC, completed apprenticeship, or relevant degree) or at least 1 year’s hands-on workshop experience.

- A practical approach and a strong problem-solving mindset for mechanical and electrical challenges.

- The ability to work from engineering information such as assembly instructions, 2D drawings, and 3D CAD models.

- Confidence using workshop and power tools safely.

- A keen eye for detail, both when following processes and when helping improve them.

- Clear communication and a collaborative approach.

- Willingness to travel within the UK and Europe, typically around once a month.

- Availability for weekend installations roughly every other month, with time off in lieu.

- Living within commuting distance of Stratford, London, and the right to work in the UK.

Nice to have

- Electrical, wiring, or software knowledge.

- Experience installing industrial equipment, or working in warehouse, manufacturing, or recycling environments.

- Experience operating industrial robots or automated systems.

- A full UK driving licence.

postings.title: Machine Learning Engineer
postings.description:
A little bit about us 

At Recycleye we are revolutionising recycling. Our ground-breaking AI-powered robots and optical sorters are making waste sorting faster, cleaner and more profitable. With our advanced tech, the previously unsortable can now be sorted efficiently and effectively. Founded in 2019, we have grown rapidly ever since, with installations at leading waste management companies across Europe and the US. 

We are on a mission to help our clients produce higher quality outputs – turning the world’s waste into valuable resource. And our work has never been needed more. Worldwide only 9% of plastic waste is being recycled – every day, we are proud to work on making a meaningful difference towards a sustainable future. 

Be part of it – come and join us! 

Why choose to work at Recycleye? Our team works together to grow and succeed, driven by our shared values of ambition, curiosity, customer centricity, integrity and respectful ideation. We offer great benefits, built-in upskilling and unlimited holiday. 

We know that our mission will be achieved by having the most passionate, driven, talented, and all-around best people on our team. So come and help us shape the future! 

What you'll work on 

Our team develops new features across Recycleye’s waste sorting and plant monitoring products, improving the end-to-end performance of our systems. That might mean evaluating and deploying new model architectures, adapting ideas from ML papers to our use cases, implementing novel object tracking algorithms, diving deep into camera optics and calibration, or making our DeepStream pipelines more efficient. Everything we build runs in production on real sorting lines, so we look for the solution that works best for the problem, which might mean stepping back and choosing a better camera rather than chasing a cool new model. 

You will be a core member of a small, high-impact ML R&D team. Building new features and developing better ways to measure how well our products perform, whether that’s sorting a waste stream or understanding what’s in it, and how real site conditions affect that performance. You will work closely with our data team, who train models day to day for client projects and rely on the tools we build, and with colleagues developing a new plant monitoring product. You will also help support our deployed systems and spend time on site, getting hands-on with the waste they sort. 

As the team develops, you will help shape how we work, from code review to testing, and take on more responsibility for planning and decision-making. Along the way you will build a deep understanding of our products and the waste sorting industry, keep up with advances in computer vision, and share what we learn across the company. 

We work mostly in Python, with some Go, deploying models and algorithms to NVIDIA Jetson devices running DeepStream pipelines, supported by Docker, GitHub Actions and Azure. 

What success looks like 

- Your work regularly reaches production and makes a measurable difference to how our products perform. 

- You bring new ideas to the table, test them, and help shape what we build next. 

- You grow into owning technical areas of our systems, and become a trusted reviewer and planning partner for the team. 

- Teams across the company, from data to install and support, know to come to you, and you help them get the best from our systems. 

- Our ways of working and measuring performance keep improving, so that our systems get better with every deployment. 

What you'll bring 

We’re looking for someone who is proactive, driven and practical, comfortable with change, and keen to learn. We don’t expect you to be an expert in everything on day one. 

- Hands-on computer vision experience, with a background in ML, physics, maths, engineering or computer science. 

- Around 3-5 years’ experience writing production-quality code, primarily in Python, and promoting good engineering practice. 

- A track record of shipping ML into production in a commercial setting, ideally including computer vision on edge devices. 

- Solid software engineering fundamentals: tested code, version control and code review. 

- Clear communication with both technical and non-technical colleagues, and a collaborative approach. 

- Comfort working independently and as part of a small team. 

- Creative, practical problem solving. 

- A love of seeing your work in the real world. You’ll spend time on site and at our demo centre, testing in challenging environments and getting hands-on with the waste our systems sort. It’s the best way to understand the problem you’re solving. 

Nice to have 

We don’t expect you to have all of these, and we’ll help you build the rest: 

- Models: computer vision detector-classifier models (YOLO, RF-DETR), segmentation models 

- Algorithms: multi-object tracking, camera calibration, homography transforms 

- Edge deployment: NVIDIA Jetson, DeepStream / GStreamer 

- Infrastructure: Docker, CI/CD (e.g. GitHub Actions), cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP, etc.) 

- MLOps: model evaluation and monitoring in production 

- Programming languages: Go 

- Tooling: building tools used by other teams 

- Hardware: physical systems or robotics, cameras and lenses 

- Commercial awareness: understanding how technical choices affect customers and the business 

What we offer 

- Day 1 health insurance through Vitality  

- Unlimited holiday 

- £1,000 professional development budget per year  

- Monthly team socials 

- Direct influence over technical direction 

Practicalities 

Location: Stratford E15 2HU, Hybrid working 

Travel: Occasional to Europe or US 

Even if you don’t tick every box listed above but are motivated by our work and believe you can make a difference on our team, we’d really love to hear from you – so please do apply and drop us a note about what you bring!

postings.title: Senior Software Engineer
postings.description:
A little bit about us   

At Recycleye we are revolutionising Recycling. Our ground-breaking AI powers robots and optical sorters making waste sorting faster, cleaner and more profitable. With our advanced tech, the previously unsortable can now be sorted efficiently and effectively. Founded in 2019, we have grown rapidly ever since, with installations at leading waste management companies across Europe and the US. We are on a mission to help our clients produce higher quality outputs – turning the world’s waste into valuable resource. And our work has never been needed more. Worldwide only 9% of plastic waste is being recycled – every day, we are proud to work on making a meaningful difference towards a sustainable future.

About the Role

Part of a larger product team we're a small software group building the software control systems for waste separation systems deployed in Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs). Our stack spans low-latency Go services, GStreamer video pipelines, real-time Python data processing, Azure infrastructure, Linux systems and Python web applications. We're looking for a developer skilled in either Python or Go who is comfortable working on the entire stack even when that means learning new things.

You'll own problems end to end - from kernel-level performance tuning to the web dashboard a client uses, to the operator interface of our industrial units. Priorities change, deadlines are often tight but the work is varied and always interesting.

What You'll Work On

- Low-latency services in Go - real-time data and control paths that minimise latency and jitter.

- Video processing - building, debugging and optimising GStreamer pipelines; camera integration, encoding/decoding, streaming and capture.

- Cloud infrastructure on Azure - VMs, container apps, deployment, networking, storage, monitoring.

- Linux sysops - provisioning and maintaining edge Linux machines: networking, systemd, containers, performance tuning, remote access and recovery. We use Ansible, Tailscale

- Python - internal tools, operator interfaces, APIs and data pipelines.

- Hands-on work - occasional hands-on work with conveyors, robotic pickers and air-jet ejection hardware.

- Graphical Interfaces - Industrial touchscreen HMI.

What We're Looking For

- 8+ years commercial software engineering experience - you have shipped and supported production systems.

- Recent experience taking your own work from design through to production, and the self-direction to deliver it with minimal oversight.

- You are happy to learn whatever is required to tackle varied technical problems, often beyond the scope of traditional software roles.

- Strong Linux fundamentals (or a desire to learn) and comfort on the command line.

- Experience with at least two or three of: Go, GStreamer, Azure (or AWS/GCP), Python, real-time or latency-sensitive systems.

- Proven ability to work effectively in a very small team - self-directing, pragmatic about trade-offs, and able to deliver under deadline pressure without disappearing down rabbit holes.

- Willing and able to travel to operational industrial sites and get hands-on with physical equipment.

- Right to work in the UK.

Nice to Have

- Experience with industrial or embedded systems, PLCs, fieldbus protocols or machine vision.

- Understanding of electronics; Microcontrollers, PCBs.

- Computer vision / ML inference deployment at the edge.

- Experience with databases, relational and columnar. We use Postgresql and Clickhouse.

- An ability to problem solve under pressure when providing second-line support.

- Opinionated about how the team works; Our processes, planning and tools.

What We Offer

- Day 1 health insurance through Vitality 

- Unlimited holiday

- £1000 professional development budget per year 

- Direct influence over technical direction.

- Work on a product with a tangible physical output. It is satisfying to see your code sorting material on a live plant floor.

Practicalities

- Occasional UK site visits to MRFs.

- Support rota but not 24/7 and never client facing.
